predecessors.name: Huns
predecessors.text: the Gepid heartland north of the Danube, 'a large part of the former Roman province of Dacia': Transylvania, the Banat, Crisana and the Tisza plain (the Cliopatria 510 shape without the Sirmium…

successors.name: Avar Khaganate
successors.text: most of the Gepid kingdom, overrun by the Avars in 567

successors.name: Lombards
successors.text: the western Gepid lands, held by the Lombards in 567-568

successors.name: Eastern Roman Empire
successors.text: Sirmium, kept by the Byzantine troops

ledger.x: 454: Ardaric founds the Gepid kingdom in the lands of the Danube and the Tisza after the Hunnic defeat at Nedao.
536: the Gepids take Sirmium from the Byzantines.
539: the Gepids hold the Danube bank round Singidunum.
555: the Gepids lose the Danube bank round Singidunum in Cliopatria's data.
565: war with the Lombards breaks out again.
567: the war ends with the Gepids beaten.
567: the Lombards take the western Gepid lands.
567: the Avars overrun the rest of the Gepid kingdom.

wars.name: Battle of Nedao
wars.outcome: The Germanic peoples under Ardaric defeated the sons of Attila; Ardaric founded the Gepid kingdom.

wars.name: Ostrogothic recovery of Sirmium
wars.outcome: Theodoric's comes Pitzia expelled the Gepid troops from Sirmium and the Ostrogoths 'recovered Pannonia' (504-505).

wars.name: Gepid-Byzantine conflict over Sirmium and Moesia
wars.outcome: The Gepids took Sirmium (536/537) and in 539 plundered Moesia; the Romans paid and 'recognize[d] new zones of Gepid occupation'.

wars.name: Lombard-Gepid war (549-552)
wars.outcome: The Lombards, allied with Justinian from 551, 'inflicted a disastrous defeat on the Gepids at the Battle of Asfeld in 552'; Thurisind lost his eldest son Turismod.

wars.name: Lombard-Gepid war (565-567)
wars.outcome: Alboin's Lombards and the Avars destroyed the Gepid kingdom in 567; Cunimund was killed and the Avars took the Gepid lands.

certainty.note: A tribal kingdom on the Danube and Tisza plains; the frontier with the Eastern Roman Empire on the Danube is approximate and its position round Singidunum changes with the wars.
